**DR31** is a medical diagnosis code used in the Danish healthcare system to classify "blood in the urine without further specification" (*blod i urinen uden nærmere specificering*) [^src1] [^src2]. Within the context of the Danish Clinical Quality Database for Atrial Fibrillation, managed by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), DR31 plays a specific role in monitoring patient safety and treatment outcomes [^src1]. 

Specifically, DR31 is utilized in the clinical quality indicator that tracks the incidence of severe bleeding among patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]] [^src1]. Because bleeding is a major risk associated with the anticoagulant medications used to treat atrial fibrillation, the database employs a comprehensive set of diagnosis codes to capture all severe bleeding events [^src1]. DR31 is grouped under the category of urinary tract and lung bleeding, alongside related codes such as [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], and [[dr04|DR04]] [^src1]. This is part of a broader monitoring framework that also tracks intracranial bleeding (e.g., [[di60|DI60]] to [[ds066|DS066]]) and gastrointestinal bleeding (e.g., [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] to [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] and [[dk92-0|DK92.0]] to [[dk92-2|DK92.2]]) to ensure standardized data collection and regional comparison across Denmark [^src1]. The code's definition and application are consistently documented in the database's annual methodology reports, including the 2023 and 2024 publications [^src1] [^src2].

## Claims
- For incidens af alvorlig blødning anvendes en bred vifte af diagnoser, herunder DI60–DS066 for intrakraniel blødning, DK25.0–DK29.8A og DK92.0–DK92.2 for gastrointestinal blødning samt DJ942, DN02, DR04 og DR31 for urinvejs-/lunge blødning [^src1] (di60, di61, di62, ds064, ds065, ds066, dk25-0, dk25-2, dk25-4, dk25-6, dk26-0, dk26-2, dk26-4, dk26-6, dk27-0, dk27-2, dk27-4, dk27-6, dk28-0, dk28-2, dk28-4, dk28-6, dk29-0, dk29-8a, dk92-0, dk92-1, dk92-2, dj942, dn02, dr04, dr31)
